objective: Run the Woodward and Colella double Mach reflection, a Mach 10 shock meeting a 30 degree ramp, on the proven density based compressible line at two grid resolutions, and gate the self similar primary triple point trajectory angle against the published reference computations at a tolerance declared before any solve
rationale: The compressible line is the lab's most proven stack: the supersonic exact theory suite passed all three gates with surface pressure within 0.07 percent of oblique shock theory, and the hypersonic blunt body family reached both gates against the Billig correlation within 2.33 percent, all on the same shipped density based solver run natively. Double Mach reflection is the canonical stress test of a shock capturing scheme on a genuinely two dimensional unsteady shock structure: two triple points, a slip line, and a near wall jet whose resolution separates dissipative schemes from sharp ones. The lab has never run it and the repository has zero hits for it. Prediction, written before any solve: the primary triple point trajectory angle lands within the declared tolerance at both rungs with the fine rung closer, and the near wall jet is visibly damped at the coarse rung, because the central upwind flux is more dissipative than the reference's PPM. The known instrument risk is the locator: the supersonic suite's own record says shock angle detection from smeared fields was its weak spot at 2 to 4 percent, so the locator increment is stated and checked against the tolerance before the first solve, per the case selection charter's detector first rule. Axis A: 3.0 gain points over 20 core minutes. Axis B: none at first filing; a clean pass is a candidate row against a published benchmark computation with no experimental anchor. Axis C: zero, no scored column moves
gate: Declared before any solve: the reference trajectory angle extracted from the published reference with its provenance tier, the tolerance on it, and the locator increment in degrees at each resolution. PASS if the measured self similar trajectory angle lands inside the tolerance at both rungs and the fine rung error is not larger than the coarse rung error. FAIL, reported as a result, if either rung lands outside with a locator increment smaller than the tolerance. NO VERDICT, at zero solves, if the locator increment at the fine rung cannot express the tolerance, per the detector first rule
cost_basis: estimate anchored to measured siblings: the hypersonic blunt body rungs on the same solver ran at single digit core minutes per mesh at comparable cell counts, and the 20 prices two rungs of an explicit two dimensional Euler solve near sixty thousand and a quarter million cells, plus margin for the acoustic time step at Mach 10; no double Mach history exists in the lab, so the figure is an estimate and is graded against the measured cost afterwards per the charter's factor three rule
expected_knowledge_gain: Three distinguishable outcomes, each changing a decision. A pass extends the compressible credential line from steady shock positions to an unsteady self similar shock structure, and the case becomes the standing regression anchor for any future flux or limiter change on the compressible stack. A fail on the trajectory angle with a clean locator is a real finding about the central upwind flux on strong unsteady reflections and bounds what the lab may claim for the supersonic line. A no verdict at zero solves means the locator cannot express the tolerance, which prices the detector work this family needs before it can be graded at all
citations: Woodward, P. and Colella, P., The numerical simulation of two-dimensional fluid flow with strong shocks, Journal of Computational Physics 54, 115-173, 1984

launch_prompt: Double Mach reflection, Woodward-Colella 1984, on rhoCentralFoam (native openfoam2606, the F3/F4 stack -- see demo-output/website/campaign/F3_supersonic_exact_theory.md and F4_hypersonic_blunt_body.md for the proven conventions). Step 1, zero compute, BEFORE any mesh exists: write the pre-registration -- (a) choose ONE formulation and state it: inclined-shock on a rectangular domain (shock at 60 degrees to the wall starting at x0=1/6, post-shock states on left inlet and on the bottom ahead of x0, time-dependent top boundary tracking the shock -- the fiddly part) OR a physical 30-degree ramp mesh with a normal Mach 10 shock; do not run both, one variable per rung; (b) extract the reference primary triple-point trajectory angle from Woodward & Colella's own figures, state its provenance tier and digitisation uncertainty; (c) declare the tolerance and the locator increment (density-gradient shock locator; increment is set by cell size -- F3's lesson says this is the weak instrument, check it can express the tolerance at both resolutions or stop at NO VERDICT with zero solves). Step 2: coarse rung (~240x60 or equivalent, gamma=1.4, inviscid, endTime 0.2); step 3: fine rung (~960x240). Extract the triple-point trajectory from a time series of shock positions, not one frame. Report PASS/FAIL/NO VERDICT against the pre-registered gate; record the wall-jet qualitative state at each rung as the dissipation note, not as a gate. Budget 20 core-min, 4 ranks, setsid for the solves, retain logs, controlDict, and the locator script under demo-output/website/campaign/DMR_runs/ per the retained-artifact rule. Evidence file in demo-output/website/campaign/, docket update on this item.
outcome: Run 2026-08-07 against DMR_PREREGISTRATION.md (committed 74797a57 before any mesh), including the dated pre-launch amendment: the canon carries no reachable numeric triple-point band (W&C paywalled, Kemm read in full, Vevek paywalled, LAVA conventions-only, DTIC 403), so the gates stood on exact incident-shock kinematics plus structure and self-similarity detectors. Gate V PASS both rungs: Mach-10 shock position error +0.0034/+0.0040 vs +/-0.0231 (0.15%/0.17% of travel), fine rung better. Gate P2 rung-to-rung PASS: chi 9.07 vs 8.21 deg constrained (|d|=0.87<=1.5), free-slope 9.94/9.89 (0.05 deg across 2x refinement). Two clauses FAILED AS WRITTEN and stay: P1's two-kink leading-front detector (the secondary triple point lives on the reflected shock -- a registration-geometry defect; the 30-contour deliverable plainly shows the full double-Mach structure at 1/120) and P2's intercept clause (offset constant in CELLS across rungs, 21.6 vs 21.2 -- instrument threshold bias, vanishing under refinement, not a self-similarity breach). Jet clause PASS both rungs. chi published as a measurement. Cost 2.4 vs 20 filed -- the estimate graded against itself at ~8x cheap-side, outside the factor-3 rule, decomposition recorded; a 1/240 successor prices at ~15 from this measurement. Evidence: campaign/DMR_RESULTS.md, campaign/DMR_runs/.
